_comment: Hand-settled entries for tools/fff-manifest.mjs, keyed by the archived filename.
Every value here was read off the archived page's own title; nothing is invented.
Applying an override clears that post's review flags -- the override is the review.
Re-run `node tools/fff-manifest.mjs` after editing this file.

fintech-female-fridays-meet-marcia-tal-c._why: Title names two companies. The card has room for one, so it takes the first.
fintech-female-fridays-meet-marcia-tal-c.name: Marcia Tal

fintech-female-fridays-meet-danita-harri._why: The source title stops mid-phrase at 'Director of Philanthropy at'. The employer it was about to name is not recoverable from the page, so no company is claimed.
fintech-female-fridays-meet-danita-harri.name: Danita Harris

fintech-female-fridays-meet-ceo-co-found._why: Role-first title. The nickname is kept as she wrote it.
fintech-female-fridays-meet-ceo-co-found.name: Rebecca (Bec) Jones

fintech-female-fridays-meet-chair-ceo-fo._why: Name last, and the company's own name carries commas, which is what defeated the split.
fintech-female-fridays-meet-chair-ceo-fo.name: Luvleen Sidhu

fintech-female-fridays-meet-founder-ceo-._why: Interviewed twice. This is the 2025 post and keeps the bare slug; the 2022 one is suffixed.
fintech-female-fridays-meet-founder-ceo-.name: Stephany Kirkpatrick

fintech-female-fridays-meet-the-nyc-fint._why: A post about the organisation rather than one person. No role or company applies.
fintech-female-fridays-meet-the-nyc-fint.name: The NYC FinTech Women Team

fintech-female-fridays-meet-chief-market._why: Title separates the series with a comma rather than a colon, so the prefix was never stripped.
fintech-female-fridays-meet-chief-market.name: Karen Voci

fintech-female-fridays-meet-global-head-.name: Supriya Jha
fintech-female-fridays-meet-global-head-.role: Global Head of Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging

fintech-female-fridays.html._why: A second post about the team, two years before the other one. Slug is stated so the two never race for the same filename.
fintech-female-fridays.html.name: The NYC FinTech Women Team

fintech-female-fridays-kelsey-weaver-and._why: The only post about two people. Both names stay, and the slug follows them.
fintech-female-fridays-kelsey-weaver-and.name: Kelsey Weaver and Lindsay Lockhart

fintech-female-fridays-stephany-zoo-head._why: Commas belong to the role, which lists three functions. Derivation was right.
fintech-female-fridays-stephany-zoo-head.name: Stephany Zoo
fintech-female-fridays-stephany-zoo-head.role: Head of Marketing, Branding, and Communications

fintech-female-fridays-charlotte-guy-pro._why: The comma is inside the company name, not between role and company.
fintech-female-fridays-charlotte-guy-pro.name: Charlotte Guy

fintech-female-fridays-petal.html._why: A post about a company, not a profile. Kept because it was published in the category.
fintech-female-fridays-petal.html.name: Petal

fintech-female-fridays-jackie-hyland-ang.name: Jackie Hyland
fintech-female-fridays-jackie-hyland-ang.role: Angel Investor, Advisor and Head of Mexico

fintech-female-fridays-sasha-pilch-sales._why: Title names her day job and her role co-founding this organisation. The card carries the day job.
fintech-female-fridays-sasha-pilch-sales.name: Sasha Pilch

fintech-female-fridays-lauren-crossett-e._why: Interviewed twice. The 2023 Pinwheel post keeps the bare slug; this earlier one is suffixed with its year.
fintech-female-fridays-lauren-crossett-e.name: Lauren Crossett
